levelling.title: Levelling
levelling.help: One levelling engine runs at a time: the regular AGC + Multiband chain (with the per-band Expander and Band Limiter inside the multiband stage) or Advanced Dynamics, which replaces all four. The pages of the engine not in use are hidden.

model.overviewHelp: Pick the station's Format Profile and the levelling engine, then check every stage at a glance. Click a card to open its page; the switch on a card turns the stage on or off.

rds.sub: Turn RDS on and see what is on air.
rds.title: Status
rds.help: Turns the RDS subcarrier on or off and shows what is on air now. TA, TP and MS are the switches an operator changes during the day. Every RDS setting applies live.

rds.sub: Station code, programme type and station name.
rds.title: Identity
rds.help: Who the station is: the PI code from your broadcasting authority, the programme type (PTY), the extended country code (ECC), four 8-character station names (PS) and the 32-character Long PS. Language, PIN, PTYN and decoder information are under Advanced. Everything applies live.

rds.sub: Radiotext messages, RT+ and now playing.
rds.title: Radiotext
rds.help: Up to 64 characters of Radiotext, with RT+ tags so receivers can show artist and title. Manual messages rotate on a timer; the now-playing script fills the {artist} and {title} macros.

rds.sub: Other frequencies that carry this programme.
rds.title: Alt. Frequencies
rds.help: Alternative frequencies let a receiver move to a stronger transmitter carrying the same programme. Method A lists every frequency in the network (up to 25); Method B pairs each alternative with the tuned frequency (up to 12 pairs).

rds.title: Schedule
rds.help: Which RDS groups go on air and how often, and the clock time (CT) with its time zone. Automatic scheduling follows the standard group rates for the features you enable.

rds.title: Subcarrier
rds.help: How much deviation the 57 kHz RDS subcarrier takes. 2.0 kHz is typical; the subcarrier is locked to three times the pilot. A change applies after an engine restart.

stages.help: Basic programme conditioning ahead of the dynamics: mono mode, the input high-pass filter, the programme lowpass and an HF trim shelf. Bypass is in the toolbar; pre-emphasis is on Audio I/O.
stages.sub: Mono, input filters and HF trim.
stages.title: Basics

stages.help: An all-pass phase rotator that makes asymmetrical waveforms, voice especially, more symmetrical without changing the tonal balance. That frees 3 to 4 dB of headroom for the dynamics stages that follow.
stages.title: Phase Rotator

stages.help: Wideband automatic gain control: rides the long-term level so quiet and loud sources reach the multiband at a similar loudness. It sets the platform; it is not the final loudness stage.
stages.sub: Slow wideband levelling ahead of the multiband.
stages.title: AGC

stages.help: Four-band parametric EQ (low shelf, two peaking bands, high shelf) on left and right, ahead of the multiband. Use it for station-wide tonal shaping.
stages.sub: Four-band tone shaping ahead of the dynamics.
stages.title: Parametric EQ

stages.help: Multiband compressor that splits the programme into 3 or 5 bands, each with its own gain ride. It is the main control for loudness and tonal density.
stages.title: Multiband

stages.help: A single-stage leveller that replaces both the AGC and the multiband compressor with one 5-band stage, so levelling and density shaping never fight. Set the sound you want (target, balance, density); the stage adapts its own speed to the programme.
stages.sub: Single-stage leveller that replaces AGC and Multiband.
stages.title: Advanced Dynamics

stages.help: Per-band downward expander: lowers the gain when a band falls below the threshold, so background noise is not lifted while programme material passes untouched.
stages.title: Expander

stages.help: Fast per-band peak limiter after the multiband compressor. It catches peaks inside each band before the bands are recombined, so the multiband can be driven harder without overshoot.
stages.sub: Per-band peak limiter after the multiband.
stages.title: Band Limiter

stages.help: PrimeBass adds perceived bass through harmonic synthesis while lowering the true low-frequency peak, which saves headroom downstream. Mono Bass sums left and right below a chosen frequency so sub-bass side energy cannot waste deviation or upset mono compatibility.
stages.title: PrimeBass

stages.help: Oversampled clipper on the low band, after PrimeBass. Use it when kick drums and bass lines still push into the limiters that follow.
stages.title: Bass Clipper

stages.help: Oversampled audio-band clipper with distortion cancellation. It cleans up audio peaks before pre-emphasis adds its high-frequency boost.
stages.title: Audio Clipper

stages.help: Rides only the pre-emphasis boost: when a cymbal or hi-hat overshoots after pre-emphasis, it briefly loses part of its boost instead of the Audio Limiter pulling the whole mix down. Gain-riding, so it adds no clipping distortion. The top octave above 13 kHz has its own, tighter threshold.
summary: thr {hf_limiter_threshold_db} dB - top {hf_limiter_top_threshold_db} dB - max {hf_limiter_max_reduction_db} dB
stages.title: HF Limiter

stages.help: Oversampled true-peak limiter on left and right, linked, with look-ahead and a high-frequency transient detector. It catches the peaks that get past every stage upstream before the audio is encoded.
stages.sub: True-peak limiter ahead of the stereo coder.
stages.title: Audio Limiter

stages.help: The stereo encoder: L+R plus L-R on the 38 kHz subcarrier, with the pilot and RDS added after all peak control. Stereo encoding is always on; the optional SSB mode leans the subcarrier towards single sideband to reclaim composite headroom ahead of the clipper.
stages.sub: Pilot-locked stereo encoder with an SSB option.
stages.title: Stereo Coder

stages.help: Oversampled clipper on the assembled composite and the main loudness control in MPX Output. It keeps clipping distortion out of the pilot, the stereo subcarrier and the RDS band so receivers decode cleanly.
stages.sub: Clips the composite while protecting pilot, stereo and RDS.
stages.title: Composite Clipper

stages.help: Holds the average multiplex power over any 60 seconds at or below the ITU-R BS.412 limit. A standards implementation for regulators that enforce BS.412; leave it off where it does not apply.
stages.title: BS.412

stages.help: Final Drive sets how hard the audio hits the composite clipper: the primary loudness control. The Broadcast Preset sets the AGC target and Final Drive together. The safety limiter on the final multiplex catches what remains while pilot and RDS stay at a constant level. Deviation and output level are on Audio I/O.
stages.sub: Final drive, broadcast preset and safety limiter.
stages.title: Loudness and Output

tools.sub: Line-up tone that replaces the input.
tools.title: Test Tone
tools.help: A line-up generator for calibrating levels and deviation. While it is on, the tone replaces the input and bypasses the processing chain, so its level arrives at the output unchanged.

tools.sub: Operating mode, devices and level calibration.
tools.title: Audio I/O
tools.help: Choose the operating mode, the input and output devices and the listening monitor, then calibrate the levels. Input Gain, Output Level and Line Output are rig calibration, remembered per device: profiles, presets and page resets never change them. Device, channel, sample-rate and block-size changes restart the engine.

tools.sub: Eight slots that save and recall the whole sound.
tools.title: Presets
tools.help: Save the current settings to one of eight slots and load them back later. Devices, level calibration and the operating mode stay as installed.

model.overviewSub: Format profile, levelling engine and every stage at a glance.
model.monitoringSub: Live levels, headroom and stream health.
model.monitoringHelp: Everything on air at a glance: levels, modulation, gain reduction, subcarriers and stream health. The Levels, Spectrum and Scopes windows show the same signals larger.

bs412_ceiling_dbr.help: Average power of the complete multiplex, pilot and RDS included, over any 60 seconds. 0 dBr IS the ITU-R BS.412 limit (the power of a sine at 19 kHz deviation); lower values keep a margin below it.
bs412_ceiling_dbr.label: Ceiling

multiband_link_strength.help: How much the left and right channels share one gain reduction in each band. 0 = each channel compressed on its own, 1 = fully linked (stereo image held exactly).
multiband_link_strength.label: Stereo Link

processed_audio_coder_has_clipper.label: External Coder Has Its Own Clipper
